note: Reference roster, not live data. Roles only; no holdings figures are stated here. The live US ownership split comes from FRED on the Bonds tab.

players.name: Bank of Canada
players.role: Sets the overnight target rate and can buy or sell Government of Canada securities for its own balance sheet.
players.why: Its policy rate anchors the front end of the curve; prime and variable mortgages move with it.

players.name: Government of Canada (Finance Canada)
players.role: Issuer of the benchmark 2, 3, 5, 7, 10 and 30-year bonds.
players.why: Auction sizes and the deficit shape supply, which feeds into yields.

players.name: Bank-owned dealers
players.role: RBC Capital Markets, TD Securities, BMO Capital Markets, Scotiabank, CIBC Capital Markets and National Bank Financial are among the main distributors and market-makers.
players.why: They bid at auctions and quote the market that mortgage pricing is based on.

players.name: Pension and public investors
players.role: CPP Investments, CDPQ, Ontario Teachers', OMERS and similar long-horizon funds.
players.why: Large, patient buyers of long bonds; their demand affects the long end.

players.name: CMHC and Canada Mortgage Bonds
players.role: CMHC runs the Canada Mortgage Bond programme that funds insured mortgages.
players.why: CMB spreads over Government of Canada bonds feed through to insured fixed mortgage rates.

players.name: Foreign investors, insurers and asset managers
players.role: Hold a large share of Government of Canada debt alongside domestic institutions.
players.why: Foreign demand and global rate moves, especially US Treasuries, spill into Canadian yields.

players.name: Federal Reserve
players.role: FOMC sets the fed funds target range; the Fed also holds Treasuries on its balance sheet.
players.why: Policy path and balance-sheet runoff or purchases move Treasury yields, which Canadian yields track.

players.name: US Treasury
players.role: Issuer of Treasury bills, notes and bonds.
players.why: Refunding announcements and auction sizes drive supply.

players.name: Primary dealers
players.role: A couple of dozen banks and broker-dealers designated by the New York Fed that must bid at Treasury auctions and trade with the Fed.
players.why: They intermediate the market and absorb supply that end investors do not take.

players.name: Foreign official and private holders
players.role: Japan, the UK and China have been among the largest foreign holders.
players.why: Shifts in foreign demand can move term premia.

players.name: Money-market funds, mutual funds, pensions, banks
players.role: The domestic private holders of Treasuries.
players.why: Their allocation changes with yields, deposit flows and regulation.
